newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dlr regains upper hand for new bull run.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dlr regains upper hand for new bull run.

text.p: The dollar got an unexpected boost from a surge in expectations of an imminent rate hike and is set to attack several resistance levels, technical analysts said on Thursday.
"Dollar/mark is going to go higher, to 1.6950 and than 1.70 the figure," said I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden, who noted the dollar took 1.6850-mark near-term resistance easily on Thursday.
In late trading, the dollar was quoted at 1.6925/35 marks versus 1.6800/05 at the close on Wednesday, and at 123.65/70 yen vs 122.79/84.
"Dollar/yen may be a little different," Morden also said. "Today's price action really confirms dollar/yen is still continuing higher."
Analysts said dollar/yen tested a four-month uptrend line in the 122 to 121.80 area. The fact this area held indicates there still is scope for a run all the way to 124.82, the high on February 14.

"Dollar/yen is turning positive on divergence studies, which is possibly a strong buy signal. We should test 124.82 next week, and, if that's the case, even test 126.20 in the next two to three weeks," Morden added.
Analysts agreed the dollar, helped by the U.S. interest rate outlook, is the leader in this fresh rally which should cap mark/yen strength between 72.80 and 73.30.
As for dollar/Swiss, having taken out a tough resistance at 1.4480, it seemed headed for a test of 1.4585 and then 1.4625.
Dollar/Swiss was quoted in late trade at 1.4530/40 versus a close on Wednesday at 1.4420/30.
